questions.text:
For a C program accessing x[i][j][k], the following intermediate code is generated by a compiler. Assume that the size of an integer is 32 bits and the size of a character is 8 bits.
t0 = i * 1024
t1 = j * 32
t2 = k * 4
t3 = t1 + t0
t4 = t3 + t2
t5 = x[t4]
Which one of the following statements about the source code for the C program is CORRECT?
questions.solution:
t2 = k [latex]\times[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] element size 4 bytes (int).
t1 = j [latex]\times[/latex] 32 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] one row of the last dimension = 32 B = 8 ints [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] third dimension 8.
t0 = i [latex]\times[/latex] 1024 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1024 / 32 = 32 rows [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] second dimension 32.

So x is int x[ ][32][8], which matches int x[32][32][8].

Answer: int x[32][32][8]

options: x is declared as "int x[32] [32] [8]".
x is declared as "int x[4] [1024] [32]".
x is declared as "char x[4] [32] [8]".
x is declared as "char x[32] [16] [2]".

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT performed during compilation?
questions.solution:
Type checking, symbol table management and inline expansion are all done by the compiler.

Dynamic memory allocation (malloc/new) happens only when the program runs.

Answer: Dynamic memory allocation

Type checking
Symbol table management
Inline expansion

questions.text:
Consider the grammar defined by the following production rules, with two operators * and +
S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T *P
T [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]U| T*U
P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q +P |Q
Q [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Id
U [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Id
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]T\rightarrow T*U[/latex] is left recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] * is left associative.
- [latex]P\rightarrow Q+P[/latex] is right recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] + is right associative.

Answer: + is right associative, while * is left associative

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]+[/latex] is left associative, while * is right associative
[latex]+[/latex] is right associative, while * is left associative
Both + and * are right associative
Both + and * are left associative

questions.text:
A canonical set of items is given below
S[latex]\rightarrow L. \gt R[/latex]
Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R.
On input symbol [latex]\lt [/latex] the set has
questions.solution:
The item S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] L. [latex]\gt[/latex] R shifts only on "[latex]\gt[/latex]", so there is no shift on "[latex]\lt[/latex]". The set has just one complete item (Q [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R.), so there cannot be two reductions. No conflict on "[latex]\lt[/latex]".

Answer: neither a shift-reduce nor a reduce-reduce conflict

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: a shift-reduce conflict and a reduce-reduce conflict.
a shift-reduce conflict but not a reduce-reduce conflict
a reduce-reduce conflict but not a shift-reduce conflict.
neither a shift-reduce nor a reduce-reduce conflict

questions.text: Which one of the following is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Replacing x = 4 * 5 by x = 20 computes the constant at compile time: that is constant folding, not common subexpression elimination. The other statements are true.

Answer: x = 4*5 [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] x = 20 is an example of common subexpression elimination (FALSE)
